correctness.rationale: Exact multiplicative divisor-sum identity, reduction modulo Q of all possible odd-divisor subsets, integer bound 1<=R<=Q+2<2Q, and reduction modulo odd prime p force precisely the internal prime powers, then force p=2^(k+1)-1. Converse substitution is exact. Executed an exact brute-force subset verifier over 1,680 parameter triples and 243,840 candidate subsets (21 matching), independent of the proof; source code and expected output supplied. No finite run is claimed to prove the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The 2023 primary source restricts its new two-deletion classifications to prime exponent 1 or 2; the subsequent full two-deletion classification for exponent >=3 proves exactly the m=3 Mersenne case and does not cover all-odd sets of three or more omitted divisors. Our new content treats every exponent >=4 (three or more forced odd omissions) and gives one global uniqueness theorem. Searches of related published indexed claims and accessible earlier claims found no implication-equivalent stronger covering result. A cited 2016 thesis not accessible in full is recorded as a specific residual literature risk.
residual_risks: Full text of Adajar (2016) thesis was not obtained; possible equivalent theorem cannot be decisively excluded.

value.rationale: All-odd omission sets form a canonical and motivated stratum of the near-perfect divisor problem on 2^k p^e. The result is an exact complete classification of every such subset and every exponent, forces Mersenne support, proves uniqueness and determines a sharp size e-1 that grows without bound. Its e>=4 classification goes beyond known one- and two-omission results, not merely finite numerical data or a relabeled special case.
